The '''2020–21 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was coached by [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]], who was in his 18th and final season as UNC's head men's basketball coach. The Tar Heels played their home games at the [[Dean Smith Center]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the 18–11, 10–6 in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place. As the No. 6 seed in the ACC Tournament, they defeated [[2020–21 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] and [[2020–21 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]], before losing to [[2020–21 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] in the semifinals. North Carolina received an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 8 seed in the Midwest region. They lost in the first round to 9th-seeded [[2020–21 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].

On February 27, 2021, Roy Williams won his 900th career game in a win over Florida State, becoming the 5th and fastest Division I men's head coach to reach the milestone. On March 6, 2021, UNC completed a season sweep over rival [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in a 91–73 win. Following the win, Roy Williams kissed the Smith Center court, causing speculation of possible retirement. Williams later said it was because of the team's 10–1 home record.<ref>{{Citation|title=Roy Williams Explains Kissing Center Court|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fygr6-Az76A|language=en|access-date=2021-04-03}}</ref>

Following the season, Williams announced he was retiring after 18 years as head coach of North Carolina and 33 years of coaching.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-01|title=UNC icon Roy Williams retiring after 33 seasons|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31177433/north-carolina-tar-heels-basketball-coach-roy-williams-retires|access-date=2021-04-01|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-01|title=UNC's Williams retires: 'No longer the right man'|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31177433/north-carolina-tar-heels-basketball-coach-roy-williams-retires|access-date=2021-04-07|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> Several days later, the school named assistant coach [[Hubert Davis]] as the team's new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pickman|first=Ben|title=UNC Hires Hubert Davis as Next Head Coach|url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/04/05/hubert-davis-north-carolina-tarheels-head-coach-roy-williams-successor|access-date=2021-04-07|website=Sports Illustrated|language=en-us}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|Tar Heels]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 14–19, 6–14 in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in three-way tie for last place. As the No. 14 seed in the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2019–20 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] before losing to [[2019–20 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] in the second round. All postseason tournaments, including the remainder of the ACC Tournament, the [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], and [[2020 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] were canceled due to the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships}}</ref><ref name="ACC Tournament">{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref>

==Rankings==
{{See also|2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings}}

On January 18, 2021, Duke fell out of the AP Top 25 ranking for the first time since February 8, 2016. This broke a 59-year streak and marked the first time since [[1961–62 NCAA University Division men's basketball rankings|December 25, 1961]] that the powerhouse trio of Duke, Kentucky and North Carolina were all out of the Top 25 ranking.<ref>{{cite web|author=Cassandra Negley|title=Duke, UNC, Kentucky all outside of men's AP Top 25 for first time since 1961|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa-basketball-duke-unc-kentucky-out-of-mens-ap-top-25-for-first-time-since-1961-201005754.html|date=January 18, 2021|access-date=January 20, 2021}}</ref>
